entries.old: With Node available, drive BUILD and PROVE with `run-engine.mjs`: bind the approved DAG at approval (`DAG_BOUND`), run `init` then `drive`, and read only `status`. Record RED, review and ship-ready with `run-engine.mjs gate red|review|ship-ready --repo <dir> --ticket <key> --run-id <id> --input <json-file>` rather than hand-run loops; a `gate review` FAIL enqueues its finding-bound repair, which the next `drive` dispatches. With `config.unitReview`, record each unit's independent review with `gate unit-review` first ([review.md](references/review.md), Unit review); unit reviews do not replace the final review, which stays mandatory and names `units_consumed`. Judgment points (`status.judgments`) come back to you or the user. The manual flow below is the documented fallback when the engine or gate module is unavailable (record `harness degraded`). A run that falls back after `init` stays manual for the rest of the ticket: do not `resume`, `drive` or `gate` it again, since its ledger no longer reflects the work. While that state file exists the carrier still treats it as REPAIR authority, so a REPAIR the ledger does not authorize is **WAIT_FOR_USER**, never a hand-edit of the state file.

entries.old: `memoryBudgetMb: "auto"` takes OS free memory, capped by Node's cgroup-aware `availableMemory()` (Node >= 22). On older Node it is capped by the cgroup limit minus measured cgroup usage (`memory.current` / `memory.usage_in_bytes`). A reserve of 1 GiB or 15% of total, whichever is larger, is subtracted. If a cgroup limit exists but its usage is unreadable, the estimate is `memory_verified: false`. `memory_safety` is `estimated` only when a verified budget applied and **every** node has `estimatedMemoryMb`; otherwise it is `unverified`. Node's available/constrained probes are cgroup-aware only on Linux, so they are consulted only there. On macOS, `os.freemem()` counts only free pages (about 0.7 GB of 24 GB on the host where this was found), so the harness reads `vm_stat` and counts free, inactive, speculative and purgeable pages instead.

It may declare `redSpecs` (repo-relative spec paths); then `redEvidence` must be an absolute path to a non-empty file with the failing-run output, written by the orchestrator, or dispatch is refused.

entries.old: **Unit review (opt-in; AIS-HARNESS-3 Wave 2b-ii).** `config.unitReview: true` (boolean, needs a unit; never defaulted, so the DAG digest covers it only when set) makes each unit need its own independent review chain. The engine never dispatches a reviewer: the orchestrator relays it ([review.md](review.md), Unit review) and `gate unit-review` validates and records it under the lock, reusing `gate.mjs` `gateReview` (contract, enums, dispositions, builder roster, distinct reviewers). The input is `{unit, review_execution, kind: original|confirmation, approved_plan_digest, dag_digest, base_commit, primary, second_opinion?, reconciliation, graded_artifacts?, repair_ownership?, repair_prompt_file?}`, where the reviewers' `candidate_id` is the unit's evidence id (`status.units.<u>.evidence.id`); `--unit` may name the unit instead. It is accepted only when the unit is `verified`, nothing is live, the digests are the bound ones and the evidence id and base commit are the current evidence's. Refusals record nothing: `unit_review_disabled`, `unknown_unit`, `binding_mismatch`, `attempts_live`, `unit_unverified`, `stale_base`, `stale_evidence`, `chain_broken` (an execution id of another chain), `unit_review_current`, `unit_review_open`, `retry_unauthorized`, `repair_outside_unit`, `repair_prompt_missing`, `reviewers_same_provider`, `parent_ceiling` (not a durable judgment), and every `gateReview` refusal. A unit is risky when a member node carries a risk label or the ticket has `config.riskLabels`. Its review and its confirmation then need a second opinion (`missing_second_opinion`) from a provider other than the primary's (`reviewers_same_provider`; a CodeRabbit fallback is route `coderabbit` with identity `coderabbit:<model>`). Otherwise a second opinion is optional and validated when given. The record carries each reviewer's provider and model; model-name roles are the orchestrator's duty. The record (in `S.unit_reviews.<u>.chain`) binds the plan and DAG digests, the unit, the evidence id, its base commit and whole-tree candidate (`tree_candidate`), the reviewers, findings and outcome. The review state is recomputed at every read against the current evidence: `unreviewed`, `pass`, `stale` (the reviewed evidence no longer holds: a fresh original is due), `fail` awaiting `repair|recheck|confirmation`, or `fail` terminal (computed judgment `unit_review_terminal`). An accepted FAIL with findings to fix, before the freeze, enqueues `repair-<rx>` (kind `unit-review`) through the review-repair authorization (the FAIL record in the unit's chain, `rounds.unit_review_repairs`, finding-bound writes that must lie inside the unit's declared writes); `drive` dispatches it only while the unit's evidence is the reviewed one (else `UNIT_REPAIR_CANCELLED`), records it in the unit chain without freezing and re-checks the unit. The new evidence becomes the candidate of the one targeted confirmation only when, against the binding the FAIL reviewed, nothing but files inside the repair write set changed (`UNIT_REPAIR_BOUND`). A declared directory is compared file by file against its tree recorded at the FAIL, so a repair writing `src/a.txt` inside a declared `src` binds, while any other changed, added or removed entry inside it is outside the repair. A node re-run, a dependency unit's re-check, an upstream change or a base move instead marks the repair `unbound` (`UNIT_REPAIR_UNBOUND`) and the review stale. This bookkeeping is idempotent and runs on every `drive`, `resume`, `status` and gate, so a crash between a re-check and its binding is recovered. A failed confirmation, an overflow FAIL, a FAIL with nothing to fix, a failed repair, a FAIL whose cycle the ceiling cannot carry (`ceiling_refused`, recorded with `repair_opened: false`) and any FAIL after the freeze are terminal: only a trusted RUN-STATE `RETRY {review_execution, predecessor: <the unit's last execution>, authorized_by}` admits a new original. A re-review, a repair and a confirmation spend the parent-wide ceiling. Opening a repair needs 3 unheld slots: it spends 1 and holds its re-check and confirmation for the unit until the cycle ends or is cancelled (`UNIT_CEILING_RELEASED`). The spends are recorded (`UNIT_REVIEW_CYCLE` with kind `unit_rereview|unit_repair|unit_confirmation` and its trigger: stale evidence and its invalidation causes, the owner RETRY, the fixed findings, the repair). `gate review` (original and confirmation) and `gate ship-ready` refuse `unit_reviews_missing` until every unit has a current PASS (and `gate review` the two Wave 3 refusals below). The `drive` outcome `done` does not cover pending unit reviews; `status.unit_reviews_pending` is authoritative. The carrier's REPAIR authorization also reads the unit chains, but only a FAIL whose repair the engine opened (`repair_opened: true`).

entries.old: **Final review on unit evidence (AIS-HARNESS-3 Wave 3; only with `config.unitReview`).** Unit reviews do not replace the final review ([review.md](review.md), Final review on unit evidence). After the refusals above, `gate review` also refuses, recording nothing: `acceptance_uncovered` when an original's `primary.acceptance_criteria` has no row whose `id` (when that is an acceptance id; else its `criterion`: one row covers one id) is an acceptance id mapped on a node (every id of `config.acceptanceIds`), and `units_consumed_stale` when an original or a confirmation does not name, in the input field `units_consumed: [{unit, evidence_id}]`, every unit exactly once with its current verified evidence id (`status.units.<u>.evidence.id`): a missing, unknown, duplicated or old entry is refused. The accepted record carries `units_consumed`, and `gate ship-ready` re-checks the record that authorizes ship (the last accepted original or confirmation) by the same rule, refusing `units_consumed_stale` when a unit's evidence moved since (for example the resolved base moved and the units were re-checked and re-reviewed on a byte-identical candidate). `init` refuses (`dag_invalid`) `config.unitReview: true` without `config.acceptanceIds`. Without `config.unitReview` none of this runs and `units_consumed` is a usage error (exit 1), so the final review is unchanged.

entries.old: **`gateRed`** is a scheduler prerequisite: a node whose dependency has `redSpecs` is not dispatched until RED is accepted, repairs included. The engine runs the DAG-bound runner itself: `gate red` input is `{node, command?, specs?}`, where `command` only names a formatted `config.testCommands` entry; the command, its format, the timeout and the node's `resources` never come from the input. It runs with a bounded timeout, its own process group and the resource locks under the same durable attempt protocol as workers, so a surviving runner holding a lock is reconciled, not re-run. A runner (RED or proof) is `exited` only after its whole group is proven gone; a group that survives the kill, or whose quiescence is unknown, leaves the attempt `unknown` with its locks held and returns `quiescence_unknown` (judgment point) with no evidence or proof recorded. When a runner changes the approval binding (plan narrative or DAG bytes), its result is dropped (`RED_DROPPED`) and the binding code is returned as a judgment point; the binding is re-verified before RED evidence or local proof is committed, so drifted evidence never reaches disk. Runners (RED, proof and unit checks) run repository commands with the engine's own, unmodified environment, API keys included: the billing strip above applies to provider workers only. Runner adapters (`parseRunnerOutput`): `node --test` TAP (including nested subtests), vitest JSON, jest JSON. RED needs every named spec to report an **assertion** failure; import, compile and collection errors do not count. A spec matches a result by name and file; a result without a file counts only when no other result has that name and, if it failed, no other failure carries a location (so another file's same-named failure never makes RED). A runner that rewrites a named spec file (a snapshot update) is refused as `spec_rewritten`: the spec digests are taken before the runner starts. Unsupported output cannot establish RED: that is a judgment point and the manual flow applies, marked degraded. Evidence is bound to the spec files' content digests, the baseline candidate and the resolved `config.base` commit, ordered by event sequence, and is refused if recorded after a dependent production dispatch. Before a drive dispatches a dependent (or repair) that needs it, a changed spec digest or a moved `config.base` drops the evidence (`RED_INVALIDATED`, kept in `gates.red_invalid` with the old evidence) and the engine re-runs RED itself with the recorded runner and specs, once per invalidation (`RED_RERUN`; it ignores dispatches before the invalidation). The `red_invalidated` judgment names the re-run's attempt and outcome. Accepted: that drive stops, the next one dispatches. Refused (typically `spec_not_failing`, because dependents already implement the specs): every later `drive` and `status` reports it until `gate red` is accepted, or the spec files and `config.base` are restored to the old evidence's bytes (`RED_RESTORED`); otherwise the owner decides. A dependent's own writes never invalidate it.

entries.old: **`gateShipReady`** emits `SHIP_READY` only when the current candidate equals the reviewed one, the exclusions are unaltered, graded artifact digests still match, the review chain is accepted, every required node is done or cancelled, no attempt is live, no repair is open, no judgment is unresolved (`nodes_unfinished`, `attempts_live`, `repairs_open`, `judgments_unresolved`), local proof is bound to that candidate, and every required risk evidence is present (a `-spec` kind needs accepted RED on that file; any other kind must name an existing file inside the repository, checked by the engine). Local proof is produced by the engine running every `config.testCommands` entry (exit 0 = pass) under the runner protocol; an input `local_proof` is a usage error. A proof command that changes the work tree is refused as `candidate_mismatch` and its proof is bound to no tree (`local_proof.candidate_id: null`, `dropped: ["candidate_mismatch"]`), so a RETRY review of the tree it left still needs a proof of that tree; one that changes the approval binding (the excluded plan narrative or the DAG bytes) is refused with that binding code and its proof dropped; no `SHIP_READY` is recorded. With units, the unit conjuncts are re-checked after the proof ran: a proof command that leaves the tree but makes unit evidence stale (for example an empty commit moving `config.base`) is refused with the existing code (`units_unverified`, `unit_reviews_missing` or `units_consumed_stale`) and its proof dropped; the next `drive` re-checks the units (spending rechecks), and the proof command must be fixed or it moves the base again on the next ship-ready. A proof runner without proven quiescence records no proof and leaves a durable `quiescence_unknown`. Overflow on either reviewer makes PASS `outcome_inconsistent`. Remote CI is still checked afterwards, as today. No successful closure is ever synthesized.

entries.old: **Who.** An Opus primary reviewer that is independent of every builder, under the rules in this file. The gate refuses a reviewer whose identity equals a builder's. A **risky** unit (`status.units.<u>.review.risky`: a member node carries a risk label, or the ticket has `config.riskLabels`) also needs a second opinion from a provider other than the primary's (Codex for the Opus primary, whatever the host: on a Codex host the counterpart Claude would share the primary's provider and is refused), on its review and on its confirmation. If the counterpart is unavailable or its usage limit is reached, run CodeRabbit on the unit's paths and record it as route `coderabbit` with identity `coderabbit:<model>`. If neither can run, stop and ask (`WAIT_FOR_USER`); never record the risky unit without it. For a risky unit the gate requires the second opinion to come from a different provider than the primary (`reviewers_same_provider`) and records each reviewer's provider and model. It does not check model names: assigning Opus as primary and Codex as second is the orchestrator's duty under the owner rule. For a unit that is not risky the second opinion is optional; when it is given, the gate validates it.

entries.old: **Input.** Give the reviewer the unit's exact files and diff (its nodes' declared reads and writes), its acceptance ids, the contract versions it reads, its check results, the approved plan and the threat model. The artifact uses the output contract above, with `candidate_id` set to `status.units.<u>.evidence.id`. The gate input adds `unit`, `approved_plan_digest`, `dag_digest` and `base_commit` (`status.units.<u>.evidence.base_commit`). Record it with `run-engine.mjs gate unit-review --input <file>`. Use a unique `review_execution` for each unit review (`review-<opaque>`); the final review may not reuse it.

entries.old: **FAIL and repair.** Reconcile as above. An accepted FAIL with `fix` findings needs `repair_prompt_file` and opens one repair. Its write set (the fixed findings' paths plus `repair_ownership`) must lie inside the unit's declared writes; anything outside is `repair_outside_unit`, so leave that finding to the final review: record the unit review with that finding dispositioned to the final review (for example `final-review`, never `fix`) and its rows judged on the unit alone, so the unit can PASS (a unit FAIL with nothing to fix is terminal), then carry the finding into the final review as a primary finding to `fix`, whose one repair may cross units. `drive` runs the repair only while the unit's evidence is still the one that was reviewed; otherwise it cancels the repair and the review goes stale. Then `drive` re-checks the unit. The re-checked evidence becomes the repaired candidate only when the repair's own writes are the sole change; a node rebuild, a dependency unit's re-check or any other change makes the review stale instead, so a fresh review is due. The same primary (plus the second opinion when the unit is risky) then gives one targeted confirmation on the repaired evidence (`kind: "confirmation"`). Each unit review execution gets one repair and one confirmation. The following are terminal for the unit (`unit_review_terminal`): a failed confirmation, an overflow FAIL, a FAIL with nothing to fix, a failed repair, a FAIL the ceiling cannot carry, and any unit FAIL after the REVIEW freeze (after the freeze, only the final review's repair may change the candidate). Only an owner RUN-STATE `RETRY` linked to the unit's last execution continues, never an automatic retry.

entries.new: **`gateRed`** is a scheduler prerequisite: a node whose dependency has `redSpecs` is not dispatched until RED is accepted, repairs included. The engine runs the DAG-bound runner itself: `gate red` input is `{node, command?, specs?}`, where `command` only names a formatted `config.testCommands` entry; the command, its format, the timeout and the node's `resources` never come from the input. It runs with a bounded timeout, its own process group and the resource locks under the same durable attempt protocol as workers, so a surviving runner holding a lock is reconciled, not re-run. A runner (RED or proof) is `exited` only after its whole group is proven gone; a group that survives the kill, or whose quiescence is unknown, leaves the attempt `unknown` with its locks held and returns `quiescence_unknown` (judgment point) with no evidence or proof recorded. When a runner changes the approval binding (plan narrative or DAG bytes), its result is dropped (`RED_DROPPED`) and the binding code is returned as a judgment point; the binding is re-verified before RED evidence or local proof is committed, so drifted evidence never reaches disk. Runners (RED, proof and unit checks) run repository commands with the engine's own, unmodified environment, API keys included: the billing strip above applies to provider workers only. Runner adapters (`parseRunnerOutput`): `node --test` TAP (including nested subtests), vitest JSON, jest JSON. RED needs every named spec to report an **assertion** failure; import, compile and collection errors do not count. A runner that rewrites a named spec file (a snapshot update) is refused as `spec_rewritten`: the spec digests are taken before the runner starts. Unsupported output cannot establish RED: that is a judgment point and the manual flow applies, marked degraded. Evidence is bound to the spec files' content digests, the baseline candidate and the resolved `config.base` commit, ordered by event sequence, and is refused if recorded after a dependent production dispatch. Before a drive dispatches a dependent (or repair) that needs it, a changed spec digest or a moved `config.base` drops the evidence (`RED_INVALIDATED`, kept in `gates.red_invalid` with the old evidence) and the engine re-runs RED itself with the recorded runner and specs, once per invalidation (`RED_RERUN`; it ignores dispatches before the invalidation). The `red_invalidated` judgment names the re-run's attempt and outcome. Accepted: that drive stops, the next one dispatches. Refused (typically `spec_not_failing`, because dependents already implement the specs): every later `drive` and `status` reports it until `gate red` is accepted, or the spec files and `config.base` are restored to the old evidence's bytes (`RED_RESTORED`); otherwise the owner decides. A dependent's own writes never invalidate it.

entries.new: `memoryBudgetMb: "auto"` takes OS free memory, capped by Node's cgroup-aware `availableMemory()` (Node >= 22). On older Node it is capped by the cgroup limit minus measured cgroup usage (`memory.current` / `memory.usage_in_bytes`). A reserve of 1 GiB or 15% of total, whichever is larger, is subtracted. If a cgroup limit exists but its usage is unreadable, the estimate is `memory_verified: false`. Node's available/constrained probes are cgroup-aware only on Linux, so they are consulted only there. On macOS, `os.freemem()` counts only free pages (about 0.7 GB of 24 GB on the host where this was found), so the harness reads `vm_stat` and counts free, inactive, speculative and purgeable pages instead.

entries.new: **Unit review (opt-in; AIS-HARNESS-3 Wave 2b-ii).** `config.unitReview: true` (boolean, needs a unit; never defaulted, so the DAG digest covers it only when set) makes each unit need its own independent review chain. The engine never dispatches a reviewer: the orchestrator relays it (Unit review, below) and `gate unit-review` validates and records it under the lock, reusing `gate.mjs` `gateReview` (contract, enums, dispositions, builder roster, distinct reviewers). The input is `{unit, review_execution, kind: original|confirmation, approved_plan_digest, dag_digest, base_commit, primary, second_opinion?, reconciliation, graded_artifacts?, repair_ownership?, repair_prompt_file?}`, where the reviewers' `candidate_id` is the unit's evidence id (`status.units.<u>.evidence.id`); `--unit` may name the unit instead. It is accepted only when the unit is `verified`, nothing is live, the digests are the bound ones and the evidence id and base commit are the current evidence's. Refusals record nothing: `unit_review_disabled`, `unknown_unit`, `binding_mismatch`, `attempts_live`, `unit_unverified`, `stale_base`, `stale_evidence`, `chain_broken` (an execution id of another chain), `unit_review_current`, `unit_review_open`, `retry_unauthorized`, `repair_outside_unit`, `repair_prompt_missing`, `reviewers_same_provider`, `parent_ceiling` (not a durable judgment), and every `gateReview` refusal. A unit is risky when a member node carries a risk label or the ticket has `config.riskLabels`. Its review and its confirmation then need a second opinion (`missing_second_opinion`) from a provider other than the primary's (`reviewers_same_provider`; a CodeRabbit fallback is route `coderabbit` with identity `coderabbit:<model>`). Otherwise a second opinion is optional and validated when given. The record carries each reviewer's provider and model; model-name roles are the orchestrator's duty. The record (in `S.unit_reviews.<u>.chain`) binds the plan and DAG digests, the unit, the evidence id, its base commit and whole-tree candidate (`tree_candidate`), the reviewers, findings and outcome. The review state is recomputed at every read against the current evidence: `unreviewed`, `pass`, `stale` (the reviewed evidence no longer holds: a fresh original is due), `fail` awaiting `repair|recheck|confirmation`, or `fail` terminal (computed judgment `unit_review_terminal`). An accepted FAIL with findings to fix, before the freeze, enqueues `repair-<rx>` (kind `unit-review`) through the review-repair authorization (the FAIL record in the unit's chain, `rounds.unit_review_repairs`, finding-bound writes that must lie inside the unit's declared writes); `drive` dispatches it only while the unit's evidence is the reviewed one (else `UNIT_REPAIR_CANCELLED`), records it in the unit chain without freezing and re-checks the unit. The new evidence becomes the candidate of the one targeted confirmation only when, against the binding the FAIL reviewed, nothing but files inside the repair write set changed (`UNIT_REPAIR_BOUND`). A declared directory is compared file by file against its tree recorded at the FAIL, so a repair writing `src/a.txt` inside a declared `src` binds, while any other changed, added or removed entry inside it is outside the repair. A node re-run, a dependency unit's re-check, an upstream change or a base move instead marks the repair `unbound` (`UNIT_REPAIR_UNBOUND`) and the review stale. This bookkeeping is idempotent and runs on every `drive`, `resume`, `status` and gate, so a crash between a re-check and its binding is recovered. A failed confirmation, an overflow FAIL, a FAIL with nothing to fix, a failed repair, a FAIL whose cycle the ceiling cannot carry (`ceiling_refused`, recorded with `repair_opened: false`) and any FAIL after the freeze are terminal: only a trusted RUN-STATE `RETRY {review_execution, predecessor: <the unit's last execution>, authorized_by}` admits a new original. A re-review, a repair and a confirmation spend the parent-wide ceiling. Opening a repair needs 3 unheld slots: it spends 1 and holds its re-check and confirmation for the unit until the cycle ends or is cancelled (`UNIT_CEILING_RELEASED`). The spends are recorded (`UNIT_REVIEW_CYCLE` with kind `unit_rereview|unit_repair|unit_confirmation` and its trigger: stale evidence and its invalidation causes, the owner RETRY, the fixed findings, the repair). `gate review` (original and confirmation) and `gate ship-ready` refuse `unit_reviews_missing` until every unit has a current PASS (and `gate review` the two Wave 3 refusals below). The `drive` outcome `done` does not cover pending unit reviews; `status.unit_reviews_pending` is authoritative. The carrier's REPAIR authorization also reads the unit chains, but only a FAIL whose repair the engine opened (`repair_opened: true`).

entries.new: **Final review on unit evidence (AIS-HARNESS-3 Wave 3; only with `config.unitReview`).** Unit reviews do not replace the final review (Final review on unit evidence, below). After the refusals above, `gate review` also refuses, recording nothing: `acceptance_uncovered` when an original's `primary.acceptance_criteria` has no row whose `id` (when that is an acceptance id; else its `criterion`: one row covers one id) is an acceptance id mapped on a node (every id of `config.acceptanceIds`), and `units_consumed_stale` when an original or a confirmation does not name, in the input field `units_consumed: [{unit, evidence_id}]`, every unit exactly once with its current verified evidence id (`status.units.<u>.evidence.id`): a missing, unknown, duplicated or old entry is refused. The accepted record carries `units_consumed`, and `gate ship-ready` re-checks the record that authorizes ship (the last accepted original or confirmation) by the same rule, refusing `units_consumed_stale` when a unit's evidence moved since (for example the resolved base moved and the units were re-checked and re-reviewed on a byte-identical candidate). `init` refuses (`dag_invalid`) `config.unitReview: true` without `config.acceptanceIds`. Without `config.unitReview` none of this runs and `units_consumed` is a usage error (exit 1), so the final review is unchanged.

entries.new: **Who.** An Opus primary reviewer that is independent of every builder, under the rules in [review.md](review.md). The gate refuses a reviewer whose identity equals a builder's. A **risky** unit (`status.units.<u>.review.risky`: a member node carries a risk label, or the ticket has `config.riskLabels`) also needs a second opinion from a provider other than the primary's (Codex for the Opus primary, whatever the host: on a Codex host the counterpart Claude would share the primary's provider and is refused), on its review and on its confirmation. If the counterpart is unavailable or its usage limit is reached, run CodeRabbit on the unit's paths and record it as route `coderabbit` with identity `coderabbit:<model>`. If neither can run, stop and ask (`WAIT_FOR_USER`); never record the risky unit without it. For a risky unit the gate requires the second opinion to come from a different provider than the primary (`reviewers_same_provider`) and records each reviewer's provider and model. It does not check model names: assigning Opus as primary and Codex as second is the orchestrator's duty under the owner rule. For a unit that is not risky the second opinion is optional; when it is given, the gate validates it.

entries.new: **Input.** Give the reviewer the unit's exact files and diff (its nodes' declared reads and writes), its acceptance ids, the contract versions it reads, its check results, the approved plan and the threat model. The artifact uses the output contract in [review.md](review.md), with `candidate_id` set to `status.units.<u>.evidence.id`. The gate input adds `unit`, `approved_plan_digest`, `dag_digest` and `base_commit` (`status.units.<u>.evidence.base_commit`). Record it with `run-engine.mjs gate unit-review --input <file>`. Use a unique `review_execution` for each unit review (`review-<opaque>`); the final review may not reuse it.

entries.new: **FAIL and repair.** Reconcile as in [review.md](review.md). An accepted FAIL with `fix` findings needs `repair_prompt_file` and opens one repair. Its write set (the fixed findings' paths plus `repair_ownership`) must lie inside the unit's declared writes; anything outside is `repair_outside_unit`, so leave that finding to the final review: record the unit review with that finding dispositioned to the final review (for example `final-review`, never `fix`) and its rows judged on the unit alone, so the unit can PASS (a unit FAIL with nothing to fix is terminal), then carry the finding into the final review as a primary finding to `fix`, whose one repair may cross units. `drive` runs the repair only while the unit's evidence is still the one that was reviewed; otherwise it cancels the repair and the review goes stale. Then `drive` re-checks the unit. The re-checked evidence becomes the repaired candidate only when the repair's own writes are the sole change; a node rebuild, a dependency unit's re-check or any other change makes the review stale instead, so a fresh review is due. The same primary (plus the second opinion when the unit is risky) then gives one targeted confirmation on the repaired evidence (`kind: "confirmation"`). Each unit review execution gets one repair and one confirmation. The following are terminal for the unit (`unit_review_terminal`): a failed confirmation, an overflow FAIL, a FAIL with nothing to fix, a failed repair, a FAIL the ceiling cannot carry, and any unit FAIL after the REVIEW freeze (after the freeze, only the final review's repair may change the candidate). Only an owner RUN-STATE `RETRY` linked to the unit's last execution continues, never an automatic retry.

entries.new: **`gateShipReady`** emits `SHIP_READY` only when the current candidate equals the reviewed one, the exclusions are unaltered, graded artifact digests still match, the review chain is accepted, every required node is done or cancelled, no attempt is live, no repair is open, no judgment is unresolved (`nodes_unfinished`, `attempts_live`, `repairs_open`, `judgments_unresolved`), local proof is bound to that candidate, and every required risk evidence is present (a `-spec` kind needs accepted RED on that file; any other kind must name an existing file inside the repository, checked by the engine). Local proof is produced by the engine running every `config.testCommands` entry (exit 0 = pass) under the runner protocol; an input `local_proof` is a usage error. A proof command that changes the work tree is refused as `candidate_mismatch` and its proof is bound to no tree (`local_proof.candidate_id: null`, `dropped: ["candidate_mismatch"]`), so a RETRY review of the tree it left still needs a proof of that tree; one that changes the approval binding (the excluded plan narrative or the DAG bytes) is refused with that binding code and its proof dropped; no `SHIP_READY` is recorded. A proof runner without proven quiescence records no proof and leaves a durable `quiescence_unknown`. Overflow on either reviewer makes PASS `outcome_inconsistent`. Remote CI is still checked afterwards, as today. No successful closure is ever synthesized.
